page: Amazon Web Services c6id.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is comprised of 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface provides a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a PassMark CPU score of 88092.76 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 124962.53, both placing in the top tiers. The hardware excels in cryptographic and extended instruction tasks, as evidenced by top-tier PassMark encryption and extended instruction test results. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, reaching 335.25 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores falling into the average category.

Given its high compute density, large local NVMe storage, and 50 Gbps network bandwidth, the c6id.metal is well-suited for data-intensive, multi-threaded workloads. These include database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, where it demonstrates strong benchmark throughput. It also supports moderate LLM inference tasks, particularly for prompt processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal configuration maximizes resource density and eliminates hypervisor overhead, making it a viable option for high-throughput, localized storage-dependent enterprise applications.
